newsitem.title: UK: Dollar off highs in Europe after U.S. goods data.
newsitem.headline: Dollar off highs in Europe after U.S. goods data.

text.p: The dollar gathered momentum in late Europe and ended above 1.69 marks and 124 yen after U.S. durable goods jumped to record highs in the wake of the first U.S. rate hike in two years.

"We have shifted away from Fed watching back to economy watching and this (goods) is the first reading we have had on the economy since the rate move yesterday," David Coleman, chief economist at CIBC Wood Gundy said.
February U.S. durable goods rose 1.5 percent to record highs of $178.32 billion against forecasts for an 0.4 percent drop. While the dollar got a lift from the numbers it ended off peaks.
The dollar jumped to session peaks of 1.6955 marks after the figures, but settled off highs at 1.6920/25 marks against 1.6928/33 in late Europe on Tuesday.
Against the yen the dollar ended the session at 124.01 yen, below peaks of 124.47 yen, though up from 123.91/96 in late Europe on Tuesday.
The dollar drew little inspiration in Europe from Tuesday's widely anticipated 1/4 point rise in the fed funds rate to 5.50 percent.
